rules.title: Security Deposit Law - maximum deposit and annual increase limit
rules.requirement: A landlord may not collect a security deposit of more than one and one-half times one month's rent, and any additional yearly security deposit increase may not exceed 10% of the current security deposit. A pet security deposit may not be charged if, combined with the regular deposit, it exceeds one and one-half times one month's rent.
rules.key_value: one and one-half times one month's rent; yearly increase not to exceed 10% of the current security deposit
rules.coverage_text: Most residential rental properties, including mobile homes.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings, although a tenant in such a dwelling may make the Security Deposit Law apply to their tenancy 30 days after sending a written request to the landlord.
rules.quoted_span: The maximum-security deposit to be collected by the landlord cannot be more than one and one-half times one month’s rent ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2 ). It can be less. Any additional yearly security deposit increase may not exceed 10% of the current security deposit.

rules.title: Security Deposit Law - limit on prepaid rent at lease inception
rules.requirement: Prepaid funds held to secure future rents, including last month's rent, count as part of the security deposit. At the inception of the lease the landlord may not require more than two and one-half times the monthly rent, including the security deposit and the first month's rent.
rules.key_value: two and one-half times the monthly rent at the inception of the lease, including security deposit and first month's rent
rules.coverage_text: Most residential rental properties, including mobile homes.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings, unless the tenant makes the Security Deposit Law applicable by written request.
rules.quoted_span: The landlord may only require one and one -half times the tenant’s monthly rent as security and the first month’s rent at the inception of the lease. That means the landlo rd may not require more than two and one-half times the monthly rent at the inception of the lease, this includes the security deposit and the first month’s rent.

rules.title: Security Deposit Law - return of deposit within 30 days
rules.requirement: Within 30 days after the termination of a tenancy, the landlord must return the security deposit plus interest earned less deductions, with an itemized list of any deductions sent by registered or certified mail.
rules.coverage_text: Most residential rental properties, including mobile homes.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings, unless the tenant makes the Security Deposit Law applicable by written request.
rules.penalty: The tenant may sue and the court may award double the amount wrongly withheld, together with court costs and reasonable attorney's fees.
rules.quoted_span: Within 30 days after the termination of a tenancy, a landlord must return the security deposit, plus interest earned less deductions, to the tenant ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.1).

rules.title: Security Deposit Law - deposit account notice and interest
rules.requirement: Within 30 days of receiving the security deposit and at each annual interest payment, the landlord must notify the tenant in writing of the bank or investment company holding the deposit, the deposit amount, account type and current interest rate; interest belongs to the tenant.
rules.key_value: written notice within 30 days of receipt of the deposit
rules.coverage_text: Most residential rental properties, including mobile homes.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings, unless the tenant makes the Security Deposit Law applicable by written request.
rules.penalty: If the tenant does not receive proper notice or interest, the tenant may give written notice that the security money plus interest at 7% per annum be applied to rent.
rules.quoted_span: Within 30 days of receipt of the security deposit and at t he time of each annual interest payment, the landlord must notify the tenant in writing of the name and address of the banking institution or investment company in which the money is deposited, the amount of the deposit, type of account, and current rate o f interest for the account.

rules.title: Security Deposit Law - return on displacement
rules.requirement: Within five (5) business days after a tenant is displaced by fire, flood, condemnation, or evacuation, the landlord must return the security deposit, when a public official has posted a notice prohibiting occupancy or certified the displacement is expected to last longer than seven (7) days.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants displaced by fire, flood, condemnation, or evacuation.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings, unless the tenant makes the Security Deposit Law applicable by written request.
rules.quoted_span: Within five (5) business days after a tenant is displaced by fire, flood, condemnation, or evacuation, the landlord must return the security deposit.

rules.title: New Jersey Law Against Discrimination - source of lawful income
rules.requirement: Landlords may not discriminate in renting housing and must give equal treatment regardless of protected characteristics, including source of lawful income.
rules.coverage_text: All landlord-tenant relationships, with stated exceptions.
rules.exemptions: Two-family owner occupied dwellings, rooms in an owner or resident-occupied single home, and residences planned exclusively for and occupied by one sex; age-restricted housing as it pertains to familial status.
rules.penalty: Monetary damages, being required to rent the unit to the complainant, and fines up to $10,000 for a first offense (N.J.S.A. 10:5-14.1a(a)).
rules.quoted_span: The New Jersey Law Against Discrimination (LAD), N.J.S.A. 10:5-12(g) to -(h), prohibits discrimination when selling or renting property and requires equal treatment in the sale or rental of housing regardless of race, creed, color, national origin, ancestry, sex, marital status, civil union status, domestic partnership status, familial status, affectional or sexual orientation, gender  identity or expression, mental and physical disability, nationality, or source of lawful income.
